reason: The code comments state that tag variants must never slip money work past a human, but asserting null for 'payment' lets tasks tagged with 'payment' bypass the protected lane because DENIED_TAGS only lists the plural form.
All callers use the slug solely to construct file paths where a trailing dash causes no harm, making the truncation order a harmless edge rather than a bug.

Callers never treat 'git status --short' as valid proof for deleted work because landing-proof independently verifies changed blobs via holdsWork, and accept-verify-gate leaves non-allowlisted commands marked unchecked rather than passed.
The test pins a check that only excludes flags starting with two dashes, causing atris switch -h to look up -h as an account instead of showing the switch help supported by the router.

Stripping ticket IDs without removing enclosing parentheses leaves malformed empty parentheses that callers like clarify pass directly to user-facing output, with no comments or tests indicating this behavior is intended.
Not probing the crontab is a deliberate design choice to keep status checks fast, as explicitly enforced by the test 'autoland status never probes a stalled crontab'.
The test creates a directory with a space and asserts an unquoted cd command in the crontab line, which causes the shell to fail and breaks if quotes are added to fix it.
Resolving unparseable profile files causes the shell switch wrapper to export the profile and report a successful switch even though activation exits with an error.
All callers receive next_at through readSchedule, which requires Number.isFinite, making bad inputs a harmless edge nobody reaches.
Valid member slugs explicitly allow dots and underscores across the CLI, but ACTIVITY_LINE omits them and drops those members' live progress, which the test locks in by asserting null.
scanChatLogs omits the global option when constructing report.sources.ax_dirs, so the report and CLI output fail to list the scanned home directory despite including its sessions.
Neither campaign-schema.js nor the caller requires a human: prefix to close an ask, and openLaneAsks deliberately closes the ask on any ask_answered event regardless of actor.
buildCard renders with the fallback atris theme when given an unknown theme name but still returns the invalid theme string, causing the CLI to falsely report that the unused theme was applied.

The test title explicitly specifies that formatCents tags non-USD currencies and directly asserts '$5.00 EUR', demonstrating that appending the currency code to the formatted amount is an intentional implementation choice.

The test explicitly names this intended behavior ('an empty artifact only earns the default wiki and operator-load points'), and real callers always populate the wiki field via buildWikiArtifact which properly assigns missing status.

Splitting on newlines counts the empty string after the trailing newline as an extra line, causing businessDiff to report a two-line file as having three lines without any comments or documentation indicating this off-by-one count is intended.
The test explicitly names and tests this fallback as an intentional design choice to pick the newest starter task when a person has no matching claimed tasks.
All callers use the default prefix or provide a non-empty string, making the empty prefix a harmless edge case that no real caller reaches.

Comments in lib/engine-registry.js explicitly state hidden profiles are registered engines too, and multiple tests intentionally assert that resolveRegisteredEngine lists all registered engine ids rather than public runner profiles.

Parsing omits trailing newlines from intermediate sections while reconstructJournal joins sections without a delimiter, causing round-trip merges in log-sync and pull to glue adjacent headings like 'More## Inbox' onto a single line.

commands/run-front.js forwards --json to speakFirstMinute without setting fresh, so running atris run --json in an initialized workspace unexpectedly outputs plain text instead of JSON with no documentation or comment indicating this was intentional.

The test asserts events?days=1, which queries a rolling 24-hour upcoming window that omits earlier events today and includes tomorrow's events instead of using the local calendar day bounds defined by localDayBounds.
The label deliberately reflects the sync direction of applying web updates to the local file, while the diff output explicitly identifies the local and remote file paths.
The test explicitly documents with an inline comment that a comma ends a path but is not a valid boundary prefix for the next one, showing that dropping the unspaced second path is deliberate.
No caller programmatically parses the health property, making minor verb agreement in informational CLI status messages a matter of taste rather than a functional bug.
When allowYes is false, refuseHeadlessUnless still instructs the user to pass --yes even though it rejects that flag, locking in misleading guidance for callers like atris serve.

The test title expects reporting an empty local skills folder, but the assertion locks in an error exposing the internal '--all' default because skillFix omits the empty-folder check implemented by skillLink.
Passing duplicate --repo flags is a harmless edge case that no caller or documented usage reaches, and the test explicitly asserts first-flag resolution consistent with the rest of the module.
The test deliberately mocks broken.py with invalid JSON and asserts ok:true to verify that the batch audit catches per-service errors and completes rather than aborting.

The test asserts research_files is 3 because countFiles uses recursive readdirSync without filtering out directory entries, mistakenly counting the nest folder as a file alongside alpha.md and beta.md.

Stripping punctuation after collapsing whitespace leaves an uncollapsed double space that breaks title deduplication in callers like seedInitTaskPlane, contradicting the function's deduplication purpose and the test's own title.

The test explicitly asserts this intended behavior under the name 'starts fresh metadata when the stored metadata cannot be read', and writing valid JSON metadata naturally makes the record readable again.
The file header documents exit code 2 for bad usage, but stringsCommand unconditionally returns 0 after printing help, allowing invalid subcommands or typos in gate scripts to silently succeed.
The test comment explicitly states that pinning null for whitespace-only built_by is deliberate behavior pinned on purpose rather than an unintended bug.

The regex in taskTagTokens excludes underscores, truncating #needs_human to needs and preventing callers like isDecisionTask from detecting the decision hold despite normalizeDecisionTag explicitly converting underscores to hyphens.

The snapshot line is built as 'Team stream: 0 active agents.' and only loses 'Team' in JSON mode because stripLeadingAgent unintentionally matches the placeholder agent 'team', with no comments, callers, or tests showing this truncation was intended.
The only caller in haikuRates already skips falsy receipts with if (!receipt) continue, making verifierPassed(null) a harmless edge case that callers never reach.
The code intentionally requires a slash or dot in looksLikePath, which the audit summary confirms is a deliberate design choice and the test explicitly categorizes under malformed steps.
The test asserts that error output includes advice to set ATRIS_API_BASE, but executeAgentSDKFast hardcodes 127.0.0.1:8000 and never reads the ATRIS_API_BASE environment variable.

clipLine reserves three characters specifically to append an ellipsis, but fallbackQuestions strips trailing punctuation after clipLine instead of before, accidentally removing the ellipsis and leaving an abrupt 87-character truncation that the test locks in.
